own_solution.law: The Bateman equations give Ad(t) = A0*lambda_d/(lambda_d-lambda_p)*(exp(-lambda_p*t)-exp(-lambda_d*t)), with lambda_p = ln(2)/(66 h) and lambda_d = ln(2)/(6 h). At 24 h, Ad = A0*(11/10)*(2^(-4/11)-2^(-4)).
assumptions: Decay is exponential with constant decay constants.
Every parent decay produces the daughter.
All nuclei remain in the column during the stated run.
A further loading at the start increases the initial parent activity by the stated amount.

notes: I withdraw the pass-1 rendering_not_minimal finding: pass 2 identifies T5569 and T3269 as deliberately numeral-free controls, rather than quantitative minimal pairs. The actual claimed minimal pairs, T3A18/T0FDD and TCB75/T1787, preserve 1300 Bq and change only the intended attachment or timing. Their controls also match the stated numeral-replacement construction. All certified answers agree with the Bateman relation: further initial column activities of 680, 1300 and 2900 Bq give daughter activities of 3679.29, 4166.72 and 5424.60 Bq, respectively. Container loadings cannot affect the column under the stated model. Earlier-run loadings introduce no additional dependency because the present initial activity and absence of daughter are specified. Rates expressed per hour give dimensionless exponents and a dimensionless rate ratio, leaving the answer in Bq.
